title: Polyethylene glycol-based isolation of urinary extracellular vesicles
author: Singh, Patnam, et al.

EV Protein Marker Analysis: Following MISEV recommendations, EV-specific marker proteins were identified by western blotting analysis of the UEV isolate [2]. To obtain the total protein, isolated UEVs were harvested in RIPA lysis buffer containing protease- and phosphatase-inhibitors (G Biosciences, MO, USA) and quantified by BCA assay. 50 μg UEV protein was loaded in 10% SDS-PAGE. The protein bands were then transferred onto a nitrocellulose membrane using a wet transfer unit at 70 Vs for 2 h at 4 °C. The membrane blots were saturated for 2 h at room temperature with 5% non-fat dry milk in TBST. Following blocking, the blots were incubated overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies (Abcam, Cambridge, UK), at a ratio of 1:2000, followed by 2 h of incubation at room temperature with secondary antibodies (Abcam, Cambridge, UK), at a ratio of 1:6000. The blot was developed. Images were captured with the iBright7500 instrument (Thermo Fisher Scientific, California, USA) (Fig. 4c).

UEV RNA Extraction: Total RNA from UEV isolates was extracted using TRIzol™ LS Reagent (Invitrogen, CA, USA) following the manufacturer's instructions. Summarising, the extracellular vesicle sample and Trizol reagent (1:3) were combined and incubated for 5 min at room temperature. The mixture received a 1:5 addition of chloroform, which was then centrifuged at 12,000*g for 15 min at 4 °C. The upper aqueous phase was carefully transferred to a fresh tube. An equal volume of isopropanol and 1 μL of 500 μg/mL Glycogen (GlycoBlue™ co-precipitant Invitrogen, CA, USA) were added to each tube and incubated at −20 °C overnight. The next day, the samples were centrifuged at 12,000*g for 15 min at 4 °C, and the pellet was washed with ethanol. The RNA pellet was air-dried for a few minutes, dissolved in nuclease-free water, and stored at −80 °C for further analysis. Qubit™ RNA HS Assay Kit was used to quantify the amount of RNA (Invitrogen, CA, USA). The UEV RNA was also analysed in the Agilent Bioanalyzer 2.1 instrument using an RNA Pico kit (both from Agilent Technologies, CA, USA) (Fig. 5a). The total RNA yield was 264 ± 83.8 pg/ml of urine. Endogenous gene expression analysis: RT-qPCR was used to confirm the expression of housekeeping genes in the UEV-RNA pool [39]. 1 μg of UEV-RNA obtained from the preceding step was reverse transcribed using a High-capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA), following the manufacturer's instructions. Pre-amplified cDNA was diluted 1:5 with nuclease-free water, and 1 μL was used as a template for RT-qPCR. A 10 μL reaction was performed in the Applied Biosystems 7500 Real-Time System using 5 μL of TB Green Premix Ex Taq (Takara Bio Inc. Shiga Prefecture, Japan), 0.1 μL of a 10 μM primer pair, 1 μL of template cDNA, 3.8 μL of nuclease-free water, and a no template control. Real-time PCR was conducted for the 30 s at 95°C, followed by 35 cycles of 5 s at 95°C and the 30 s at 60°C. The cycle threshold (CT) values obtained for each housekeeping gene and the data are represented in Fig. 5b.

steps.title: Centrifuge urine to remove debris
steps.instruction: Place 1.20 mL of collected urine in an Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge (rotor F‑34‑6‑38) and spin at 3000 g for 10 min at 4 °C to pellet cells and debris.

steps.title: Adjust pH and add Tris‑EDTA buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube, adjust the pH to 4 using 0.2 N HCl, then add 5 mL of Tris‑EDTA buffer (20 mM, pH 6.8, Sigma, MO, USA).

steps.title: Vortex, centrifuge, and mix with PEG
steps.instruction: Vortex the mixture for 90 s, centrifuge at 8000 g for 15 min at 4 °C, collect the supernatant, and add an equal volume of PEG precipitation solution (24 % w/v PEG Mn6000 in 1 M NaCl, Sisco Research Laboratories, Mumbai, India) to obtain a final PEG concentration of 12 % w/v.

steps.title: Treat pellet with DTT for THP removal
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet obtained after the previous centrifugation in 500 µL of 100 mM DTT (Sigma, MO, USA) and incubate for 10 min at 37 °C.

steps.title: Centrifuge DTT pellet and combine supernatants
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the DTT‑treated pellet at 17 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C with no brake, collect the supernatant, add it to the PEG‑supernatant mixture from step 3, and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final centrifugation, resuspend and store
steps.instruction: The next day, centrifuge the combined mixture at 10 000 g for 60 min at 4 °C, discard the supernatant, resuspend the resulting UEV pellet in 300 µL PBS, note that the pellet typically has a pH of 6.62 ± 0.107, and store at –80 °C for future use.

steps.title: Western blot analysis of UEV proteins
steps.instruction: Perform western blotting on the isolated UEVs as follows:

substeps.instruction: Lyse the UEV pellet in RIPA buffer containing protease‑ and phosphatase‑inhibitors (G Biosciences, MO, USA) and quantify protein by BCA assay.
Load 50 µg of protein onto a 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel and run electrophoresis.
Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane using a wet transfer unit at 70 V for 2 h at 4 °C.
Block the membrane for 2 h at room temperature with 5 % non‑fat dry milk in TBST.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies (Abcam, Cambridge, UK) diluted 1:2000.
Incubate 2 h at room temperature with secondary antibodies (Abcam) diluted 1:6000.
Develop the blot and capture images with an iBright7500 instrument (Thermo Fisher Scientific, California, USA).

steps.title: Extract total RNA from UEVs
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA from the UEV pellet using TRIzol™ LS as follows:

substeps.instruction: Mix the UEV sample with TRIzol LS reagent at a 1:3 (sample:reagent) ratio and incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Add chloroform at a 1:5 (TRIzol:chloroform) ratio, vortex briefly, and centrifuge at 12 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh tube, add an equal volume of isopropanol and 1 µL of 500 µg/mL Glycogen (GlycoBlue™ co‑precipitant, Invitrogen, CA, USA).
Centrifuge at 12 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C, wash the RNA pellet with ethanol, air‑dry briefly, and dissolve in nuclease‑free water.
Quantify RNA using the Qubit™ RNA HS Assay Kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA) and assess quality with an Agilent Bioanalyzer 2.1 using the RNA Pico kit (Agilent Technologies, CA, USA).

steps.title: RT‑qPCR of UEV RNA
steps.instruction: Perform reverse transcription and quantitative PCR on the extracted RNA:

substeps.instruction: Reverse transcribe 1 µg of UEV RNA using the High‑capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription kit (Invitrogen, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dilute the resulting cDNA 1:5 with nuclease‑free water.

Prepare a 10 µL qPCR reaction containing 5 µL TB Green Premix Ex Taq (Takara Bio Inc., Shiga, Japan), 0.1 µL of a 10 µM primer pair, 1 µL diluted cDNA template, and 3.8 µL nuclease‑free water. Include a no‑template control.
Run the reaction on an Applied Biosystems 7500 Real‑Time System: 30 s at 95 °C, then 35 cycles of 5 s at 95 °C followed by 30 s at 60 °C.
Record the cycle threshold (C_T) values for each housekeeping gene.
